archetype.name: Rebuilding (fast-paced, veteran-led)
archetype.definition: A team coming off a 20-win season that is giving big minutes to young guards while two veteran forwards, Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr., carry the scoring, with development ahead of the standings for now.

report.headline: Randle and Porter can score; the defense and the young guards can't yet
report.take:
Brooklyn arrives at 0-3 on the back of a 20-62 season and a third straight year of decline in the site's rankings, and nothing in the first week argues the rebuild is ahead of schedule. The Net Rtg of -12.2 ranks 26th, with the offense and the defense both 23rd, and the site has them 26th of 30. What has changed is the tempo: a Pace of 103.8 is well above the league's 101.4 and far quicker than last year's 97.1. This is a younger, faster team playing more possessions, and so far that has meant more chances for opponents to score.

The defense is the story. Opponents are posting a 60.7 Opp eFG %, 29th in the league and well above the league's 52.8, hitting 40.3% from three and 72.4% at the rim. Opposing centers are scoring 26 points a game against Brooklyn, 28th, and have dished 6 assists, 29th. That fits a frontcourt graded D beyond Randle. The Nets are doing some things right: their 75.7 DRB % ranks 6th and their 16.9 Opp TOV % ranks 5th. They are finishing the stops they get. They just aren't getting enough.

The offense rests on two players. Randle has 66 points on a 64.9 TS %, the only positive BPM in the rotation at 2.1, and a +23.1 On-Off. Porter has 64 points on a 28.2 USG %. The ball-handlers are behind them. Egor Dëmin is at a 49.9 TS % and -8.6 BPM, Mikel Brown Jr. at 38 TS % and day-to-day, and the backcourt carries a D- grade. Turnovers at 15.6 per 100 plays (25th) are what you'd expect from teenagers running the offense.

What the numbers hide: the shooting is better than it should be and the defense is likely worse than it will stay. A 37.8 3P % ranks 8th, from a team that hit 34.0 last year, and the 33.7 FT Rate is far above anything in its recent history. Some of that offense will fade. Some of the 60.7 Opp eFG % will too, because nobody allows that over a season. Three games is a tiny sample. The point differential implies one win rather than zero, so the record is a shade unlucky. The underlying team still looks like a bottom-five side.

strengths.title: Randle as the offensive engine
strengths.body: Randle leads the team in minutes, points and assists with 19, and does it efficiently: a 64.9 TS % and a +23.1 On-Off. He is the one Net with a positive BPM, and the offense runs through him as both scorer and passer. The efficiency may cool, but his role as the hub looks like the most durable part of this team.

strengths.title: Threes and free throws
strengths.body: The Nets take a big share of their shots from deep, with a 3PA Rate of 45.1 (6th), and are hitting 37.8% (8th). They are also getting to the line at a 33.7 FT Rate (7th). The volume and the free throws reflect how they want to play and should mostly hold. The 3P % is well above last year's 34.0 and is the piece most likely to slide.

strengths.title: Finishing defensive possessions
strengths.body: When Brooklyn does force a miss, it secures it: a 75.7 DRB % ranks 6th. It is also forcing turnovers at a 16.9 Opp TOV % (5th), far above last year's 13.2. The rebounding fits a long-standing team habit, but the turnover forcing is new and needs more games to trust.

concerns.title: Opponents shoot at will
concerns.body: A 60.7 Opp eFG % ranks 29th, well above the league average. Opponents are hitting threes at 40.3% and finishing 72.4% at the rim. Part of that is three games of hot opposing shooting that will cool. But Brooklyn also allowed a 57.1 Opp eFG % last year with a 26th-ranked defense, so the problem is structural, not a fluke.

concerns.title: Young guards not ready yet
concerns.body: The backcourt grades D- and none of its four listed players has a positive BPM. Dëmin is at -8.6 with a 49.9 TS %, Traoré at -6, and Brown Jr. at a 38 TS % and now day-to-day. Their growth is the point of the season, but in the meantime they feed a 15.6 TOV % that ranks 25th.

concerns.title: No answer behind Randle up front
concerns.body: The frontcourt grades D, and opposing centers have scored 26 points a game, 28th in the league. Sharpe, Clowney and Wagner all carry BPMs of -6.7 or worse. Wagner's -37.6 On-Off is the starkest number on the roster, though in three games it is partly noise.

trend.note: Two competitive losses, to Charlotte and at Cleveland, were followed by a 109-136 home blowout by Indiana. Three games prove little, but the latest one was the worst.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games and Detroit; New York is the winnable one
weekAhead.body:
Four games, three on the road. Detroit (3-0, 3rd on the site) and Indiana (10th, and already winners by a wide margin in Brooklyn) are clearly better teams. Boston and New York are the realistic targets. Boston is 22nd on the site but shoots well, hitting 39.5% of its threes on a 46.3 3PA Rate, and protects the ball at an 11.6 TOV % (3rd). That cancels the one defensive weapon Brooklyn has shown and tests its leaky perimeter defense.

The season-finale of the week at New York is the clearest opening. The Knicks are also 0-3 with the league's worst offense. A Nets defense that has been shredded should look better against a team that struggles to score, though New York's 80 DRB % (2nd) means few second chances. Coming out of the week with one win would be par. Two would be a genuine sign.

keyMatchups.title: Crashing Boston's weak glass
keyMatchups.body: Boston's 67.5 DRB % ranks 27th, and its 38 rebounds a game rank 29th. Brooklyn's own offensive rebounding is average at a 27.9 ORB %, but this is the matchup where extra possessions should be available. Against a team that shoots this well from three, the Nets probably need them.

keyMatchups.title: Randle against Detroit's power forwards
keyMatchups.body: Detroit's defense is elite overall, with a 105.6 DRtg (6th). Yet power forwards have scored 38 points a game against it, the most in the league, and done well above their usual output. If Brooklyn is going to steal a game from the Pistons, it runs through Randle at the four.

keyMatchups.title: A slump-ridden Knicks offense
keyMatchups.body: New York's 102.2 ORtg and 51.1 TS % are both last in the league. That is the best chance all week for Brooklyn's defense to post a respectable night. The Knicks have also allowed small forwards 26.67 points a game, which sets up Porter.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the Opp eFG % starts to come down from 60.7. If it doesn't even against New York, the defense is as bad as it looks.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a team very close to last year's. The defense should improve from historically bad to merely bad, since a 60.7 Opp eFG % won't last. The offense should give some back as the 37.8 3P % drifts toward the low-to-mid 30s it has lived in for years. That nets out to a rating somewhere between -6 and -10, a bottom-five profile that projects to roughly 20 to 27 wins. Randle and Porter give the Nets more scoring punch than last year's league-worst offense had, which is the case for the upper end of the range.

The real variable is the guards. If Dëmin, Traoré and Brown Jr. cut the turnovers and find any efficiency, the faster pace becomes an asset rather than a way to lose by more. If they don't, and if the veteran forwards miss time, this drifts toward last season's 20-win floor.
swingFactors: How far the opponent shooting regresses

confidence.note: Three games; the shooting numbers on both ends are far from stable.
